value: This record still cannot be a review. It was written by an automated authoring pass that also wrote the records it describes, it inherits the independence limitation recorded as RSK-003, and it cannot confirm its own definitions. Nothing settled at revision 2 makes it more independent; a reader should treat the two settled items with the same suspicion as the rest.

Thirty-nine identifier strings are shared between the two profiles. Revision 2 established, per identifier, that all thirty-nine pairs are different subjects and none is a duplicate. As of amendment ID-RULE-004-A1 (2026-10-04) the corpus no longer violates ID-RULE-004 by thirty-nine or by one: the rule now requires uniqueness within a profile, which the corpus satisfies, so the sharing is a conformant state and the identifiers are unchanged by decision rather than by deferral. No rename is required and none is permitted. What remains is not an identifier defect but a reference one: roughly nine hundred prose references carry no profile qualifier and depend on the convention that an unqualified id means the synthetic_reference copy, and corpus.py reports the subset whose named id is carried by more than one live record. That is a reported finding, not a gate.

The cross-profile reuse of identifiers is still invisible to the corpus's own duplicate check, which keys on (profile, id) by design and so cannot see it. A reader who trusts the policy statement of global uniqueness over the data will still look for a single record where there are two. That is now documented with a per-identifier table rather than with a sentence, which makes it easier to check and no easier to satisfy.

Two of the six ambiguities dispositioned at revision 2 are PARTIALLY settled and one is OPEN. The safe state of FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 was shown to be two answers about two different subjects rather than one record contradicting itself, and the two records are left disagreeing on purpose; see VOC-AMB-002 for the two decisions that would settle it, of which the identifier migration is the real one. The independence verdict on the three process records needs a governance decision about whether this corpus may write 'independent' for a separation it has not tested, and no enum member exists for the state they describe. The residual-risk rename was not performed because it rewrites fifteen records and every prose reference to them.

The word 'fault' still has no definition from the standard and none is supplied here. What revision 2 added is a usage map: three senses, the field path that distinguishes them, and the fact that the corpus contains no fault artefact, no fault list, no fault status model and no fault identifier anywhere in its 300 records. That is a description of how this corpus uses the word and it must not be read as a definition; a real definition would have to come from the standard, which this corpus may not reproduce.

The counts in this record are counts of LINES matching a term, not counts of records using it, and they were not recomputed at revision 2. A record that discusses a term in prose raises the count without depending on the term, so the dependent_records lists were built from field positions rather than from these counts and are the authoritative dependency figures. Where revision 2 needed a count that mattered - the number of field sites carrying a given key, the number of records using a value set, the number of distinct families - it was enumerated from the records rather than carried forward from the 290-line prose figure, and the field families are stated instead of line counts.

The pinned documentation cross-check produced a negative result and still does: neither docs/general/safety/safety.rst nor docs/software/modules/application/soa/soa.rst at commit 308028fb contains any of these terms, and the project ships no glossary. Revision 2 added one further negative result, which is load-bearing for the safe-state decision: the word 'propulsion' occurs nowhere in the pinned tree at that commit, which is why the as_is safe state names two conditions and the synthetic_reference one names four. So there is no product-side definition of any term here to reconcile this corpus's usage against, and every definition rests on the corpus alone.

Two corrections were made to this record's own text at revision 2 and are named here so a reader who read revision 1 knows to distrust it on exactly these points: the `fault_reaction` list on the two safety concepts has four entries and not five, and the count of shared identifiers is thirty-nine and was verified by enumeration rather than carried forward.

ambiguities_resolved.convention_adopted: Read the set from the declaring record; where a measure is judged against the reaction obligation, use the synthetic_reference four-condition set, because that is the set both concepts argue against. Read a per-mode safe state from safe_state_in_this_mode and never from the goal.

evidence.establishes: The as_is set is two conditions: 'HV contactors open, charging disabled'. This is a statement about the pinned product.

The synthetic_reference set is four conditions and is the strict superset: contactors open and charging disabled, plus propulsion disabled and fault logged. FB2-SAF-FSC-000001 and FB2-SAF-TSC-000001 argue against this set, so a reaction measure judged against the corpus's own safety argument must use it.

The word 'propulsion' occurs nowhere in the pinned tree at commit 308028fb - not in src, not in conf, not in docs. The item is a battery monitoring and control unit. A safe state naming propulsion as a condition the item disables would therefore be a claim about a vehicle-level system that the pinned product does not contain, written into a record whose origin is derived from the pinned source.

The corpus's own de facto profile marker on the as_is functional safety requirements: fault_reaction.profile_basis = 'as_is'. It is what makes an unqualified identifier reference resolvable today, and it is a convention the corpus already keeps rather than one this pass introduced.

reading_a.reading: A set of two conditions: contactors open and charging disabled.

reading_b.reading: A set of four conditions, adding propulsion disabled and fault logged, and a mode-dependent condition per operating mode.

ambiguities_resolved.residual_ambiguity: The two sets are not reconciled and this record does not reconcile them. A genuine resolution needs a decision about whether the as_is profile may carry a narrower set at all, which is a content question for the records themselves.
ambiguities_resolved.what_remains_open: Which safe state the corpus should hold, and how the collision should be broken. The two sets stay as they are.
ambiguities_resolved.what_was_settled: One thing, and it is the thing that decides how to read the rest: the two sets do not belong to one record disagreeing with itself. They belong to two different subjects, which VOC-AMB-001 establishes for all thirty-nine shared identifiers. The as_is copy states what the pinned foxBMS 2 product can be made to do; the synthetic_reference copy states what the fictional reference project's own safety concepts allocate. So the instruction to make the two records agree cannot be carried out as written, and carrying it out would make one of them false.
ambiguities_resolved.what_would_settle_it: Either of two decisions, both outside this pass. (1) The identifier migration of VOC-AMB-001: if the two profiles were given distinct identifiers, the two safe states would stop sharing a name and each would be read unambiguously, with no content decision needed and no risk of one record being made false. (2) A per-profile statement on both records naming which product each set describes, which would make the record-level difference correct as it stands but would not make it correct for a reader who searches on the identifier alone. Option (1) is the real fix and it is recorded as the prerequisite.
ambiguities_resolved.why_the_convention: The two sets appear on records that share one identifier and one ASIL, so a reader cannot tell them apart from the identifier, and the narrower set understates the obligation the corpus spends most of its safety argument on. Choosing the wider set is the conservative direction: it cannot make the reaction requirement look smaller than the corpus claims it is.
ambiguities_resolved.why_the_two_directions_are_both_wrong: Widening the as_is record to the four-condition set would put 'propulsion disabled' into a record about a battery monitoring unit that the pinned source does not support. Narrowing the synthetic_reference record to two conditions would strip both safety concepts of the obligation they allocate, and FB2-SAF-FSC-000001, FB2-SAF-TSC-000001 and FB2-SAF-ITE-000001 all read that set. There is no third direction that does not require deciding which of the two subjects the corpus intends this identifier to name, and that decision is the identifier question, not the vocabulary question.

ambiguities_resolved.what_was_settled: The vocabulary is established: `safety_allocation.asil` carries the ASIL classification scale - QM, ASIL_A, ASIL_B, ASIL_C, ASIL_D - plus the schema's own enumerated absence member `not_applicable`. Three parts of the corpus's own machinery say so independently of this record: both requirement.schema.json and safety_concept.schema.json enumerate the field as exactly those six values; the asil_assignment_validator lists QM among its valid_asils; and the requirement_applicability_validator fires on `not_applicable` alone and demands an asil_justification for it, which is why a record writing QM was never caught.

ambiguities_resolved.referential_integrity_impact: None. No record, link, digest or reference moved. The new constraint was satisfied by all eleven records carrying the key when it was first run, which is the evidence that a schema written from the corpus's own practice rejects nothing the corpus does.
ambiguities_resolved.residual_ambiguity: No schema in the corpus constrains the field by record type, so a consumer that reads fault_reaction without branching gets an object where it expected a list or the reverse.
ambiguities_resolved.what_remains_open: The consumer half. Nothing yet refuses to read the key without branching on artefact_type, so a reader written against the concept shape will still break on a requirement. Recorded rather than built because no consumer of this corpus exists to be protected.
ambiguities_resolved.what_was_not_changed: No record moved a reaction and no record changed shape. That is the point of declaring the shapes rather than merging them: the requirement-side object answers 'what does this one requirement require and who owns it', the concept-side list answers 'what does this concept allocate, to which element, with what budget', and the evidence says those are two questions rather than two shapes of one answer. Collapsing the nine objects into lists would have required inventing an element_id per requirement, and on the records that set element_owns_reaction false that entry would have named the very element the concept allocates no reaction to. Widening the two concepts to objects would have deleted their allocation argument, which is the substance of both records.
ambiguities_resolved.what_was_settled: The shape is now fixed by record type in the schema that governs each type, so a consumer no longer has to know the convention to read the field. safety_concept.schema.json already constrained the concept side: `safety_strategies.fault_reaction` is an array with minItems 1 and every entry requires reaction, triggered_by, an element_id matching ^AR-[0-9]{3}$ and reaction_time_budget_ms. requirement.schema.json now declares the requirement side as a single object whose required core - reaction, triggered_by, allocated_element_id, element_owns_reaction, allocation_basis, mode_dependence, open_limits - is byte-for-byte the core all nine requirement records already carry. Every other property in the object is optional and each is present only on the records that need it, because requiring the optional ones would have forbidden a record from recording its own budget absence.
ambiguities_resolved.why_the_convention: A single shape would move five reactions in the two concept records or collapse nine objects in the requirements, and the concept records' own allocation argument depends on having one entry per element. The distinction between 'the reaction this requirement specifies' and 'the reactions this concept allocates' is real, so the two shapes are not an error in the records - they are an under-specified schema.

ambiguities_resolved.referential_integrity_impact: None. No record, link, digest or reference moved.
ambiguities_resolved.residual_ambiguity: Nothing enforces the mapping from field name to meaning. Eleven independence-keyed fields and no schema that says which meaning a given field carries, so the convention lives only in this record and in the reader's attention.
ambiguities_resolved.what_remains_open: The one genuine defect the mapping exposed, left open on purpose. process_record.accountable_role.independence carries free prose on six records while the forty-two authoring-independence sites carry a two-valued verdict. Three of the six prose values state a verdict the enum can express - the supplier quality function's independence is untested, the reuse function's cannot hold for modified drivers, the quality engineer's is stated and not achieved - and all three would convert to not_independent. The other three do not convert: the change board, the configuration control board and the problem resolution board each record that the separation holds structurally and is not tested by any check. There is no member of {not_independent, independent} for that, and adding one - a value such as structurally_independent_but_untested - is a governance decision about whether this corpus may write 'independent' for a separation it has not tested. That is a policy question and not a vocabulary one. Writing 'independent' would manufacture an assurance the record itself says is untested; writing 'not_independent' would misdescribe a separation that does structurally hold; dropping the enum member and keeping the prose would leave the same key meaning two things in one corpus, which is the condition this entry exists to remove. So the enum was not touched and the three records were not rewritten.
ambiguities_resolved.what_was_settled: The fourteen field names carrying the word are now mapped to five distinct concepts rather than four, and the mapping is recorded so it is usable rather than incidental. Enumerated from the data: (1) AUTHORING INDEPENDENCE - whether the thing that described a subject may be the thing that produced it. Carried by `independence` under `.analysis` and under `.authority_and_independence`, by `authoring_independence` under `.derivation`, and by `independence_statement`. Forty-two of these carry the two-valued verdict {not_independent, independent} and four schemas already enumerate it. (2) ORGANISATIONAL INDEPENDENCE OF A ROLE - whether a named role may approve work it produced. Carried by `accountable_role.independence` on the process records, and this is the one place the bare key carries free prose instead of the verdict. (3) BARRIER INDEPENDENCE - whether a second channel is genuinely separate from the first. Carried by `independence_note` on the concepts' architectural elements and by `independence_assumption` in the technical concept's `diagnostic_coverage_assumptions`. (4) REVIEWER INDEPENDENCE - whether a second person confirmed the work. Carried by `independent_reviewer_used`, a boolean that reads false on all three review records. (5) MEASUREMENT AND ACCOUNTING SENSES - not a concept at all but a reuse of the word for counts: `independence_requirements_enumerated` and `independence_requirements_with_evidence_in_corpus` are counts on one test measure's tolerances, and `independence_absence` is a count in a summary_by_category table. The four schemas that already enumerate the verdict are hardware_configuration_baseline, hardware_verification_plan, software_interface_specification and safety_concept; the mapping below is why those four agree and where the fifth site does not.
ambiguities_resolved.what_would_settle_it: A governance decision on the enum, taken outside this pass, and then either a third enum member or an explicit statement that the six process records are not verdicts at all.
ambiguities_resolved.why_the_convention: The four are genuinely different questions and merging them would produce a false assurance in a specific direction: an assumed barrier independence would be readable as a satisfied organisational independence. The corpus already keeps them apart on eleven field names; recording the four readings makes the separation usable rather than incidental.

ambiguities_resolved.convention_adopted: Four readings keyed on the field family: threats[].residual_risk, test_measure oracle_detail.residual_risk, excluded element residual_risk_owner, and the risk register's residual_*_exposure family.

evidence.establishes: Before this pass: {"type": "string", "minLength": 3} - a field whose sibling residual_risk_justification has minLength 15 and is where the prose belongs, while the grade field itself would have accepted anything. Now enumerated as low, medium, not_rated, the three values all eight TARA entries actually use.

Sense (1). A grade, on the corpus's own three-value scale, beside a mitigation list and a justification. This is the only family where the word is a vocabulary, and it is the one a reader reporting 'residual risk is low' is most likely to mean without saying so.

Sense (5), the one that is not a risk. The text states what the oracle cannot establish on its own - that a source-grounded oracle still rests on the correctness of the code that produces the value it checks. Reported as a residual risk, this would read as an assurance rather than a disclaimer.

The family that is not called residual risk: residual_probability, residual_impact and residual_exposure on each risk entry, plus aggregate_exposure.highest_residual_exposure. A search for the phrase residual risk finds none of it.

residual_risk_acceptance on the TARA record states in the record's own words that acceptance of its residual risks does not exist. So no family here may be reported as an accepted risk anywhere in this corpus, and enumerating the five does not change that.

field_family_to_concept_map.value_kinds: One enumeration (low, medium, not_rated), three free-prose dispositions on the three safety analyses, one free-prose validity statement on the test measures, one ordinal pair (probability, impact) on the project risk register. No two of the five convert into one another.

reading_a.reading: A security rating on a threat, on the scale low / medium / not_rated.

reading_b.reading: A limitation of an oracle, an ownership of risk outside the item, and a project-risk exposure grade - three further meanings on three field families.

ambiguities_resolved.referential_integrity_impact: None. No record, link, digest or reference moved; the new enumeration was satisfied by all eight TARA threat entries when it was first run.
ambiguities_resolved.residual_ambiguity: The project-risk grade is not even called residual risk - it is residual_exposure - so a search for the phrase finds three of the four meanings and misses the register entirely.
ambiguities_resolved.what_remains_open: The renames. Families 2, 3 and 4 carry the same key name with the same free-prose value kind but answer different questions - one failure mode's disposition, one coupling category's, one interference category's - and family 5 shares the name while meaning something else entirely. Giving them distinct names is the honest repair and it was not performed: it rewrites fifteen records, every source anchor this record and others hold into those files, and every prose sentence in the corpus that refers to a 'residual risk' of a coupling or an interference category, and a mechanical search for the phrase would then find three of the five meanings and miss the register, exactly as it does today. That is a larger change than the naming debt clears, and unlike the two schema declarations above it would move content rather than describe it. Recorded with the map so the rename is a checklist when it is done.
ambiguities_resolved.what_was_settled: The count was wrong and the corrected enumeration is five, not four, with the bare key alone carrying four distinct value kinds across five field families. ambiguities_resolved.convention_adopted: Read 'audit' in an as_is revision history as a report of an assessment whose record does not exist here, and read it in a verification or measurement record as the corpus checking itself.

reading_b.reading: The corpus tool's own consistency check on the corpus, named as such in a measurement plan and in a generated view.

reading_b.reading: The prose environment of the same record, which on at least one record names a different kind of platform from the classification - a synthetic_fixture whose environment reads 'x86_64 Linux host (simulated)'.

record_verbatim.derivation_method: For each term: (1) enumerate every line of every artefact and review record that contains the term, matched case-insensitively on word boundaries; (2) locate the lines where the term appears as a JSON key, because a key is the corpus's own act of naming something; (3) read the two or three records that carry the key in different shapes and compare them, which is where the ambiguities came from; (4) where the corpus's usage rests on the product, read the pinned blob with git show at commit 308028fb and cite that blob rather than the working tree. Counts are line counts, not record counts, and every count in this record is reproducible from the search described beside it. Definitions were written to describe usage; none was taken from the standard and none was taken from memory. Where a definition could not be evidenced, no definition is given and the term is listed in `terms_absent_from_this_corpus` with its measured count.

identifier_vocabulary.adopted_convention: Resolve an identifier as the PAIR (profile, id), never as the id alone. This is now the corpus's primary key by policy, not only by tool behaviour: amendment ID-RULE-004-A1 (2026-10-04) states that an artefact identifier is unique within its profile. Where a record is quoted without its profile, read it as the synthetic_reference copy - that is the copy every safety concept derives from and the copy every safety argument in this corpus is made against. Prefer a field that states the profile, as `profile_basis` does on the as_is functional safety requirements, over inferring it from the directory a record happens to sit in. ON THE 39 SHARED IDENTIFIERS: no rename is required and none is permitted. They were never blocked by ID-RULE-001. An earlier revision of this field said 'Do not renumber: the policy forbids renumbering established identifiers, and 39 of them are shared, so a rename is not available as a repair', which cited ID-RULE-001 and read as though a rename were unavailable in principle. It was not: it was declined on the separate and better evidence recorded at identifier_vocabulary.migration_decision_2026_10_03, namely that renaming inverts this very convention and makes roughly nine hundred unqualified references confidently wrong with no validator able to detect it. Under the amended rule the 39 are conformant, so the question of renaming them is closed rather than deferred. The full list of shared identifiers, and the point at which the rebound identifiers stop naming a stable subject, are recorded in `limitations`.
identifier_vocabulary.artefact_identifier: The string in the `id` field: the pattern FB2-<DOMAIN>-<TYPE>-<NNNNNN>, per the corpus policy's id_scheme. Since amendment ID-RULE-004-A1 (2026-10-04) it is NOT the key of a record: the key is the PAIR (profile, id). 39 identifier strings are carried by two records, one in each profile, and from FB2-VER-EXE-000004 onwards the two records are about different subjects entirely. Under the amended rule that sharing is conformant and no rename is required or permitted, but the id alone still does not resolve, so every reference and every lookup carries or infers a profile.

evidence.establishes: The identifier FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 in the as_is profile.
The SAME identifier in the synthetic_reference profile, on a record whose safe_state and degraded_state differ from the as_is copy. Two records, one identifier, different content.
FB2-VER-EXE-000004 in the as_is profile, on the AFE LTC driver execution.
FB2-VER-EXE-000004 in the synthetic_reference profile, on the independent-monitor execution. The identifier no longer names the same subject, let alone the same content.

The corpus's de facto disambiguator: the as_is requirement carries `fault_reaction.profile_basis = "as_is"`, so the record itself declares which profile it belongs to. This is a working convention and it is recorded here as one, not as something this record introduced.

ID-RULE-004 as AMENDED on 2026-10-04: 'An artefact identifier is unique WITHIN ITS PROFILE. Two records of different profiles may legitimately carry the same identifier string, and doing so is conformant, not a collision and not a defect.' The amendment, its rationale and what it supersedes are at the `amended` block on this same rule, amendment_id ID-RULE-004-A1.

migration_decision_2026_10_03.barriers_that_were_cleared_first: A previous pass declined the re-issue on a boundary and named four things outside it. Three of the four are no longer outside it and were cleared before this decision was taken. (1) docs/artifacts/README.md, which named seven of the thirty-nine in prose ranges, is editable and its figures have been re-measured. (2) The generated trees docs/artifacts/views and docs/artifacts/spec-documents, which carried 124 and 157 occurrences, are produced by two renderers that are editable and are regenerated from the corpus, so they follow the corpus automatically. (3) test_schemas.py at the repository root, named as a blocker because it names four of the identifiers, is NOT a blocker on inspection: it constructs one self-contained literal sample payload and validates it against requirement.schema.json. It never reads the corpus, never resolves an identifier against the index and asserts nothing about any corpus record, so renaming corpus identifiers cannot affect it. That claimed blocker was void. (4) The remaining out-of-scope references are 465 occurrences in graphify-out/**, which is a generated graph-tool cache and index rather than a corpus record, and 6 in openspec/**, of which four already quote the superseded revision-1 text of SCN-MUT-001's expected finding and are stale independently of any rename.
migration_decision_2026_10_03.decision: DECIDED, NOT MIGRATED, and no longer referred. Amendment ID-RULE-004-A1 (2026-10-04) adopted route (b): ID-RULE-004 is amended to state that an artefact identifier is unique within its profile, so the 39 shared identifier strings are CONFORMANT, no rename is required, and no rename is permitted. The 39 identifier strings are unchanged. This entry originally recorded the decision as referred to a governance forum; that referral is now answered. Every field below is preserved as it was written on 2026-10-03 because the evidence it contains is the evidence the decision was taken on, and each is annotated where the amendment changes what it means.
migration_decision_2026_10_03.instrument_considered: ID-RULE-003, which requires supersession, deletion and migration to be defined, and is the policy-sanctioned route for exactly this repair.
migration_decision_2026_10_03.interim_control: SUPERSEDED. The cross-profile reuse is no longer reported as a violation of ID-RULE-004, because it is conformant under amendment ID-RULE-004-A1. Reporting it would name a rule the corpus does not violate, which is wrong at any severity. The check was repurposed rather than deleted, because the signal it carried contains a real defect that the amendment does not address: approximately nine hundred prose references name an artefact identifier with no profile qualifier, and the convention that resolves them - an unqualified id means the synthetic_reference copy - is now load-bearing under the amended rule. The replacement detector reports unqualified references whose named id is carried by more than one live record, with the candidate records and the number of referring locations. It reports and does not gate, because no machine-read path is ambiguous: every id-keyed lookup resolves (profile, id).
migration_decision_2026_10_03.no_fabrication_statement: No identifier was renamed. No digest, link endpoint revision or anchor hash was re-recorded on the basis of a rename, because none happened. The clause previously recorded here, 'Nothing in this entry asserts that the identifier scheme now satisfies ID-RULE-004. It does not', is WITHDRAWN as of 2026-10-04: under amendment ID-RULE-004-A1 the scheme satisfies the amended ID-RULE-004, which requires uniqueness within a profile and permits the sharing of one string between two profiles. This is the only clause of this statement that changed. Nothing here asserts ISO 26262 conformity, certification, tool qualification, an ASPICE capability level, human approval, production authorisation or product verification credit.
what_changed_on_2026_10_04: The instrument is no longer open. 'what_would_settle_it' below named two routes; route (b) was taken and route (a) was declined on the evidence already recorded in this entry.

'instrument_considered' named ID-RULE-003. ID-RULE-003 is NOT invoked by the amendment and is not invoked now: no supersession, deletion or migration is being performed. It is named here only as the instrument that was considered and not used.

'why_the_migration_was_still_not_performed' remains the operative reason and is now permanent rather than provisional: renaming would make roughly nine hundred unqualified prose references confidently wrong with no validator able to detect it.

Reference ambiguity - unqualified references naming an id carried by more than one live record - is now the reported quantity. See identifier_vocabulary.detection_consequence in corpus-policy.json and supersession_reconciliation_2026_10_04.detection_change_below.

'no_fabrication_statement' is superseded in one clause and stands in the rest. The clause 'Nothing in this entry asserts that the identifier scheme now satisfies ID-RULE-004. It does not' is no longer true and is withdrawn. The rest stands: no identifier was renamed, no digest, link endpoint revision or anchor hash was re-recorded on the basis of a rename, and nothing here asserts conformity, certification, human approval, production authorisation or product verification credit.
migration_decision_2026_10_03.what_would_settle_it: SETTLED, 2026-10-04. What this entry asked for was 'a recorded governance decision in docs/artifacts/governance/corpus-policy.json that either (a) states ID-RULE-003 supersedes ID-RULE-001 for cross-profile collisions and authorises a migration ... or (b) amends ID-RULE-004 to state that identifiers are unique within a profile'. Route (b) was taken. Amendment ID-RULE-004-A1 amends ID-RULE-004 to per-profile uniqueness, and records its date, author, rationale, what it supersedes and the residual risk it relocates rather than removes. No further settlement is needed for the 39 identifiers, and no route remains open for renaming them short of a further recorded amendment.
migration_decision_2026_10_03.why_the_migration_was_still_not_performe: Because renaming either side silently inverts a load-bearing convention and produces wrong answers that no validator can detect. The corpus's own adopted convention, stated in this record at identifier_vocabulary.adopted_convention and at the safe_state and safety goal entries, is that an identifier quoted without its profile is read as the synthetic_reference copy - 'the copy every safety concept derives from and the copy every safety argument in this corpus is made against'. About nine hundred prose references across the record layer rely on that convention, and they are not machine-decidable: a free-text sentence carries no profile. Renaming the synthetic_reference side would therefore not make those sentences correct, it would make them resolve to the as_is copy while continuing to read as though they meant the synthetic one, and no rule would fire, because every renamed identifier would still resolve to exactly one live record. The defect being fixed is 'an unqualified reference is ambiguous, giving the reader two live candidates'. The migration would replace that with 'an unqualified reference is confidently wrong', which is a worse failure, not a better one.
migration_decision_2026_10_03.why_this_is_not_simply_a_preference: The corpus holds two committed positions on the same question and they contradict each other. This record's identifier_vocabulary.adopted_convention says: 'Do not renumber: the policy forbids renumbering established identifiers, and 39 of them are shared, so a rename is not available as a repair', citing ID-RULE-001. The task framing for this pass names ID-RULE-003 as the sanctioned instrument. Both cannot govern. Choosing between them is a governance decision about which policy rule governs identifier collisions, and it should be recorded as one in corpus-policy.json rather than settled implicitly by whichever pass ran last. This record does not settle it and does not pretend to.
migration_decision_2026_10_03.worked_counterexample: FB2-SAF-TSC-000001 is the synthetic_reference technical safety concept. At its ftti_and_timing_budget.arithmetic_check statement it asserts: 'FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 now records the 15 ms margin as well, so the two records agree and the safety goal's budget closes ... and FB2-SAF-FSR-000003 now states those three points separately as 5 ms, 35 ms and 40 ms, so the requirement and this allocation agree.' That is a quantitative claim that a fault-tolerant time budget closes with 15 ms of margin. Checked against the two candidates: the synthetic_reference copy of FB2-SAF-FSR-000003 does carry the 40 ms figure, so the sentence is TRUE of the copy the corpus means. The as_is copy of the same identifier mentions neither 35 ms nor 40 ms, so the sentence is FALSE of it. Rename the synthetic side and this safety-budget closure argument silently comes to rest on a record that does not support it, with no validator output. The same applies to FB2-SAF-SGO-000001, whose two copies hold different safe-state sets - two conditions in as_is, four in synthetic_reference - and which this record already instructs must not be merged, at VOC-AMB-002, because merging would put a vehicle-level claim into a record describing a battery monitoring unit.

per_identifier_determination.how_this_was_determined: Enumerated every corpus record, grouped its `id` field by value, and compared the two records carrying each shared string. The deciding evidence is mechanical rather than interpretive and it is the same for all thirty-nine: the `origin` field of the two records never agrees. Fourteen as_is records carry origin 'derived' and twenty-five carry 'source_observed'; all thirty-nine synthetic_reference counterparts carry origin 'synthetic'. A record whose origin is source_observed or derived reports the pinned foxBMS sources at commit 308028fb, and a record whose origin is synthetic reports a fictional reference project. No record can be both. Therefore not one of the thirty-nine pairs is a duplicate of a single subject: there are zero duplicates and thirty-nine pairs of distinct subjects sharing one identifier. Three secondary signals corroborate without deciding anything. 16 pairs share a filename and 23 share a title - 16 share both, and every one of the 39 is listed individually in the table below - which is why the collision is easy to miss on inspection: the labels are parallel because the two profiles were authored as a matched pair, not because the two records describe one thing. The label divergence was measured per pair rather than assumed, and the two signals do not start at the same place. Titles diverge earliest, at FB2-VER-EXE-000001, and every execution and test pair from FB2-VER-EXE-000001 onward carries a different title: the as_is copy of EXE-000001 is a real macOS host run of production code and the synthetic_reference copy of the same identifier is a synthetic_fixture. Filenames still coincide for EXE-000001 through EXE-000003 and diverge from FB2-VER-EXE-000004 onward, which is the point at which the identifier stops even naming the same kind of thing. The rebound spans two namespaces: FB2-VER-TMS-000004 pairs the as_is LTC 6813-1 driver communication test against a synthetic independent-monitor test, the same pairing as EXE-000004, and FB2-VER-TMS-000005 pairs the contactor-driver test against the AFE-communication test, the same pairing as EXE-000005. Seven pairs share a filename but not a title - the three FB2-SW-IMP records, EXE-000001 to 000003 and TMS-000002 - which is the signature of the two profiles having been authored as a matched pair whose filenames were kept aligned while the content diverged.
per_identifier_determination.invariant_this_pass_preserved: No record was renumbered, merged, withdrawn or superseded. All thirty-nine identifiers are exactly as they stood at revision 1 of this record. The corpus-wide invariant (profile, id) -> one record still holds, and so does id -> at most two records, one per profile. Both invariants were true before this pass and both are true after it. What is new is that the second is now documented with the evidence that it is a policy violation rather than a coincidence, and with the cost of repairing it.
per_identifier_determination.resolution_performed: NONE, deliberately, and the reason is a boundary and not a preference. Re-issuing either side of thirty-nine identifiers is the policy-sanctioned route - ID-RULE-003 requires supersession and migration to be defined, so a deliberate migration is available and is the right instrument here - but the identifiers are named outside the boundary this pass owns. docs/artifacts/README.md, which this pass may not edit, names seven of them: FB2-SAF-HAZ-000001, FB2-SAF-SGO-000001, FB2-VER-EXE-000001, FB2-VER-EXE-000006, FB2-VER-EXE-000008, FB2-VER-EXE-000012 and FB2-VER-EXE-000015, two of them inside prose ranges written as 'FB2-VER-EXE-000008...000012' and 'FB2-VER-EXE-000001...000006', and one of those sentences already qualifies the range with the words '(profile synthetic_reference)'. test_schemas.py at the repository root names four more. The generated directories docs/artifacts/views and docs/artifacts/spec-documents carry 124 and 157 further occurrences and are produced by two renderers this pass may not edit, so their content cannot be brought back into agreement with a renamed corpus. A rename performed now would leave a committed document, a root-level test and two generated trees asserting identifiers that no longer exist. That is a larger and less honest change than the ambiguity it would settle, so the re-issue is left undone and specified instead.
per_identifier_determination.what_a_migration_must_touch: Recorded so the migration is a checklist rather than a second investigation. Within the corpus and its registries: the 39 records' own `id` fields, with a supersession entry naming the retired identifier and the new one and the date and author of the move, per ID-RULE-003; every link endpoint in docs/artifacts/traceability/link-registry/ that names one of the 39, in both the source and the target slot and in the `provenance_repair.endpoint_revision_refreshes` history of each; every reviewed_ids entry and every digest_corrections entry in the review records under docs/artifacts/reviews/ that names one of the 39; every standards_mapping backing_artifact and every coverage-plan entry; and every `dependent_records` list in this record. Outside the corpus boundary and therefore not available to this pass: docs/artifacts/README.md, test_schemas.py, the generated views and spec-documents trees, and the graphify-out and graft indexes at the repository root, which hold 195 and 13 occurrences respectively and are caches rather than records. A migration owner needs those four in scope, or needs to accept that the identifiers they name go stale.
per_identifier_determination.which_side_should_move: The as_is side, if either does, and the reason is referential load rather than preference. The as_is records are the corpus's evidence-bearing profile: they are the ones whose content is anchored to the pinned source at commit 308028fb, they are the copies a reader checking a claim about the real product would land on, and the as_is functional safety requirements already carry `fault_reaction.profile_basis = "as_is"` as the corpus's own de facto profile marker. Renumbering the synthetic_reference side leaves the pinned-product account on its established identifiers and moves only the fictional project. That is a recommendation for the migration owner, not an action taken here, and it is contingent on the four out-of-boundary surfaces above being in scope.
per_identifier_determination.why_no_pair_is_a_duplicate: A duplicate would be two records asserting the same thing about the same subject, in which case one of them could be withdrawn and every reference would survive pointed at the survivor. That is not the case here. The clearest worked example is FB2-SAF-FSR-000001, which shares its filename and its title across the two profiles while its fault_reaction differs in substance: the synthetic_reference copy records a latched FAULT mode entered within a 3 ms budget, and the as_is copy records that a measurement failure carrying DIAG severity WARNING does not open the contactors while a DIAG_FATAL_ERROR entry does, at src/app/engine/config/diag_cfg.c:180 and diag_cfg.c:159-162, with the aggregation path through BMS_IsAnyFatalErrorFlagSet() at bms.c:515-531. One copy describes a fictional project and one describes the pinned code. Withdrawing either would delete an entire profile's account of a subject.

supersession_reconciliation_2026_10_04.authority_and_limits: This reconciliation is a statement about the corpus's own committed documents. It asserts no ISO 26262 conformity, no certification, no tool qualification, no ASPICE capability level, no human approval, no production authorisation and no product verification credit. This record keeps human_approval_status 'pending', production_authorized false and product_verification_credit false, and the same is true of every other record in this corpus.

detection_change_below.replaced_by: A detector for unqualified references that are ambiguous because more than one live record carries the named id. It reports each such id, the candidate records and the number of referring locations. Severity is report-only and is not gated: every id-keyed lookup in corpus.py resolves (profile, id), so no machine-read path is currently ambiguous. Reported, not failed, and the distinction is deliberate.
detection_change_below.why_not_an_error: An error would fail validate on every run. Nothing here can fail a run: the convention resolves every unqualified reference deterministically to the synthetic_reference copy, and every machine-read path resolves the pair. Raising it would be a change of policy, not a detection of a defect.
detection_change_below.why_this_is_the_right_thing_to_measure_n: The amendment does not make the corpus's records better identified; it makes the residual risk precise. Before the amendment two things were true at once - the corpus allegedly violated a policy rule, and references were ambiguous. After it, the first is false and the second is unchanged. Deleting the check would have discarded the second along with the first, which is why it was repurposed rather than removed.
detection_change_below.withdrawn: corpus.py's cross-profile identifier reuse finding. It reported the sharing of one identifier between two records of different profiles as a MEDIUM finding against ID-RULE-004. Under the amended rule that is not a violation, so reporting it as one is now false. It is not a matter of severity - a finding that names a rule the corpus does not violate is wrong at any severity.

the_decision_now_taken.authority: docs/artifacts/governance/corpus-policy.json, id_scheme.rules[3].amended, amendment_id ID-RULE-004-A1, dated 2026-10-04, author safety_engineer.
the_decision_now_taken.effect_on_document_a: SUPERSEDED IN PART. Document A's conclusion - do not renumber - is now the governing position, but for a different reason and with a different status. It is no longer a deferral of an available repair; it is the final state. The ID-RULE-001 reasoning it cited was not what blocked the rename and is withdrawn as reasoning. Document A's other assertions survive unchanged: (profile, id) is the key, an unqualified reference reads as the synthetic_reference copy, and from FB2-VER-EXE-000004 onward a shared identifier does not even name a stable subject.
the_decision_now_taken.effect_on_document_b: SUPERSEDED IN PART. Document B's referral is now answered and its route (b) is adopted. Its route (a) is declined on the evidence, not left open. Its interim control - a medium finding reporting the reuse as a violation of ID-RULE-004 - is WITHDRAWN as a violation finding, because the condition it reported is conformant under the amended rule; it is replaced by a reference-ambiguity detector, described in detection_change_below.

no_rename_required_or_permitted_for_the_.statement: No rename is required or permitted for the 39 shared identifier strings. They are CONFORMANT under amended ID-RULE-004.
no_rename_required_or_permitted_for_the_.what_would_change_it: A further recorded governance amendment. Not a maintenance action.
no_rename_required_or_permitted_for_the_.why_conformant: Each is carried by exactly one record per profile, which is precisely what per-profile uniqueness requires. No string is carried by two records of the SAME profile, which is the condition the duplicate check reports as an error; that check has never fired.
no_rename_required_or_permitted_for_the_.why_not_permitted: Permitting the rename would re-open a settled question and would disturb a conformant state. Anyone proposing to re-issue any of the 39 must cite amendment ID-RULE-004-A1 and state why a conformant state is being disturbed, because 'the policy forbids it' is no longer the reason - the policy now permits the sharing.

the_decision_now_taken.which_ruling_now_governs: The amended ID-RULE-004 governs. An artefact identifier is unique WITHIN ITS PROFILE, and two records of different profiles may legitimately carry the same identifier string. This is route (b) - the amendment FB2-SAF-VOC-000001 itself named as the cheaper and safer of the two, and the one that matches the corpus's existing behaviour.
the_decision_now_taken.why_route_b_and_not_route_a: Route (a) was to amend nothing and migrate the 39 identifiers under ID-RULE-003. It was measured and declined on evidence recorded in this record at migration_decision_2026_10_03 and repeated in CORR-COV-021.why_not_performed: renaming either profile inverts the unqualified-reference convention, so roughly nine hundred prose references would resolve to the as_is copy while continuing to read as though they meant the synthetic one, and no validator would fire because every renamed identifier would still resolve to exactly one live record. Route (a) was therefore rejected for the defect it would have created, not deferred for want of authority.

document_a.also_asserted: That the corpus violated ID-RULE-004 and therefore was not conformant.
document_a.position: 'Do not renumber: the policy forbids renumbering established identifiers, and 39 of them are shared, so a rename is not available as a repair.' This cited ID-RULE-001 and asserted that a rename was unavailable as a repair, i.e. blocked in principle.

document_b.also_asserted: That the corpus violates ID-RULE-004 thirty-nine times and a finding reports it on every run.
document_b.position: That ID-RULE-003 is the policy-sanctioned instrument for exactly this repair, and that the repair should be performed; the entry recorded route (a) as available and route (b) as the cheaper and safer alternative but adopted neither and referred the question.
document_b.where: CORR-COV-021 in docs/artifacts/governance/coverage-plan.json, fields governance_question_referred, decision and why_not_performed

what_formerly_contradicted_itself.summary: Two committed documents in this corpus held incompatible positions on cross-profile identifier reuse and neither had authority over the other. Both positions were about the same 39 identifier strings. Until 2026-10-04 the corpus was in a state where no reading of its own committed documents could make it conformant.
what_formerly_contradicted_itself.why_they_could_not_both_govern: Document A asserted the corpus was non-conformant and that no repair existed. Document B asserted the corpus was non-conformant and that a repair existed and was available. Both named the same rule text and reached opposite conclusions about it. A reader who trusted A would conclude no action was possible; a reader who trusted B would conclude the corpus had an unexercised obligation. Neither document could settle it: which policy rule governs cross-profile identifier collisions is a governance decision about the policy, and both documents are subordinate to the policy.

identifier_vocabulary.why_it_is_a_vocabulary_problem: Three distinct failures follow, and each one produces a wrong answer rather than a missing one. (1) An unqualified identifier reference is ambiguous: FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 names two safety goals whose safe states and degraded states differ. (2) An identifier can be rebound: FB2-VER-EXE-000005 is the contactor-driver host run in one profile and the AFE-communication fixture in the other, so 'FB2-VER-EXE-000005' does not even name a stable subject. (3) RESOLVED 2026-10-04, formerly open and now closed: this failure was that the corpus policy stated that identifiers must be globally unique across profiles and the corpus did not satisfy it, so a reader who trusted the policy over the data would look for a record that did not exist. Amendment ID-RULE-004-A1 in corpus-policy.json amends the rule to per-profile uniqueness, which is what the corpus already did and what the tool already enforced, so the policy and the data now agree and (3) is no longer a failure. Failures (1) and (2) are NOT resolved and are the reason this term remains a vocabulary problem: the validator resolves (profile, id) and so is blind to both, and the only thing that resolves an unqualified reference is the convention stated below.

record_verbatim.lifecycle_status_note: 'baselined' rather than 'approved' or 'reviewed': this record fixes conventions inside the corpus and has no human reviewer. It is the output of an automated authoring pass, exactly like every review record in this corpus, and automated_review_status below refers to corpus automation only.
limitations: This record still cannot be a review. It was written by an automated authoring pass that also wrote the records it describes, it inherits the independence limitation recorded as RSK-003, and it cannot confirm its own definitions. Nothing settled at revision 2 makes it more independent; a reader should treat the two settled items with the same suspicion as the rest.

Thirty-nine identifier strings are shared between the two profiles. Revision 2 established, per identifier, that all thirty-nine pairs are different subjects and none is a duplicate. As of amendment ID-RULE-004-A1 (2026-10-04) the corpus no longer violates ID-RULE-004 by thirty-nine or by one: the rule now requires uniqueness within a profile, which the corpus satisfies, so the sharing is a conformant state and the identifiers are unchanged by decision rather than by deferral. No rename is required and none is permitted. What remains is not an identifier defect but a reference one: roughly nine hundred prose references carry no profile qualifier and depend on the convention that an unqualified id means the synthetic_reference copy, and corpus.py reports the subset whose named id is carried by more than one live record. That is a reported finding, not a gate.

The cross-profile reuse of identifiers is still invisible to the corpus's own duplicate check, which keys on (profile, id) by design and so cannot see it. A reader who trusts the policy statement of global uniqueness over the data will still look for a single record where there are two. That is now documented with a per-identifier table rather than with a sentence, which makes it easier to check and no easier to satisfy.

Two of the six ambiguities dispositioned at revision 2 are PARTIALLY settled and one is OPEN. The safe state of FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 was shown to be two answers about two different subjects rather than one record contradicting itself, and the two records are left disagreeing on purpose; see VOC-AMB-002 for the two decisions that would settle it, of which the identifier migration is the real one. The independence verdict on the three process records needs a governance decision about whether this corpus may write 'independent' for a separation it has not tested, and no enum member exists for the state they describe. The residual-risk rename was not performed because it rewrites fifteen records and every prose reference to them.

The word 'fault' still has no definition from the standard and none is supplied here. What revision 2 added is a usage map: three senses, the field path that distinguishes them, and the fact that the corpus contains no fault artefact, no fault list, no fault status model and no fault identifier anywhere in its 300 records. That is a description of how this corpus uses the word and it must not be read as a definition; a real definition would have to come from the standard, which this corpus may not reproduce.

The counts in this record are counts of LINES matching a term, not counts of records using it, and they were not recomputed at revision 2. A record that discusses a term in prose raises the count without depending on the term, so the dependent_records lists were built from field positions rather than from these counts and are the authoritative dependency figures. Where revision 2 needed a count that mattered - the number of field sites carrying a given key, the number of records using a value set, the number of distinct families - it was enumerated from the records rather than carried forward from the 290-line prose figure, and the field families are stated instead of line counts.

The pinned documentation cross-check produced a negative result and still does: neither docs/general/safety/safety.rst nor docs/software/modules/application/soa/soa.rst at commit 308028fb contains any of these terms, and the project ships no glossary. Revision 2 added one further negative result, which is load-bearing for the safe-state decision: the word 'propulsion' occurs nowhere in the pinned tree at that commit, which is why the as_is safe state names two conditions and the synthetic_reference one names four. So there is no product-side definition of any term here to reconcile this corpus's usage against, and every definition rests on the corpus alone.

Two corrections were made to this record's own text at revision 2 and are named here so a reader who read revision 1 knows to distrust it on exactly these points: the `fault_reaction` list on the two safety concepts has four entries and not five, and the count of shared identifiers is thirty-nine and was verified by enumeration rather than carried forward.
record_verbatim.review_policy_interaction: This record is not a confirmation of its own content. It was authored by the same automated process that authored the records whose vocabulary it fixes, which is precisely the independence the corpus's own risk register records as absent in RSK-003. It is therefore an input to a future human review and not a substitute for one, and its own `human_approval_status` is pending. A reader who needs to know whether these conventions are right must ask a person who did not author the corpus, and this record makes no claim that such a person has.

revision_history.author: safety_engineer
revision_history.description: First issue. Authored because the coverage plan's ISO 26262 Part 1 entry had no backing artefact, and because writing it exposed that eleven terms a reader would expect to find here have zero occurrences in this corpus - which is a measured finding rather than a defect in the record. Forty-seven terms are defined here, eleven terms are recorded as absent with their measured occurrence counts, fifteen ambiguities are resolved with both conflicting readings and their locations, and the artefact identifier is recorded as a vocabulary problem in its own right because thirty-nine identifier strings are carried by two records each. Every definition is traced to a file and line in this repository; nothing is recalled from memory. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false.

revision_history.author: safety_engineer
revision_history.description: Second issue. This pass was given ownership of the corpus records, which the first pass did not have, so it could do what the first pass recorded as needing a decision it was not entitled to make. Six of the fifteen ambiguities recorded below were the ones named as unsettled at revision 1; they are now dispositioned one by one, each with the evidence that decided it and an explicit statement of what remains open. What moved, in the corpus: two schema constraints were declared, both of which the corpus already obeyed and neither of which moves a single record's content. requirement.schema.json now declares fault_reaction on a requirement as the single object the nine requirement records actually carry, which ends the condition recorded at VOC-AMB-004 that no schema constrained the field by record type. tara.schema.json now enumerates threats[].residual_risk as low, medium or not_rated, the only value set the corpus uses there, replacing an unconstrained minLength 3 that would have accepted prose. One record moved: FB2-MAN-SCO-000001 to revision 2, converting safety_allocation.asil from QM to not_applicable and adding the asil_justification that its fourteen peer records already carry. One review record moved with it, FB2-REV-000008 to revision 3, re-deriving the single digest of that artefact and keeping the superseded digest and revision in digest_corrections; no finding, disposition, scope item or checklist entry of that review moved. Nine link endpoints were advanced in the synthetic_reference cell-voltage link registry, each keeping its superseded value, the date, the author and the description of the revision passed through, and each staying change-suspect because none of them was re-examined. What did NOT move, and why, is recorded rather than glossed. The thirty-nine identifier strings that two profiles share were analysed per identifier and the analysis is settled; the re-issue itself was not performed, and the reason is a boundary rather than a preference: docs/artifacts/README.md names seven of those identifiers in prose ranges and is outside this pass's ownership, so renaming would leave a committed document asserting identifiers that no longer exist. The two safe-state sets on FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 were shown to belong to two different subjects rather than to one record disagreeing with itself, which means the instruction to make them agree would make one of them false; that one is left open with the evidence that would settle it. The bare word fault is now given a usage-keyed definition drawn from the corpus's own records, with its three senses stated and the field path that distinguishes them named, because the gap measured at revision 1 was the absence of a usage map and not the absence of evidence: three hundred and ninety occurrences were available and three of them are sufficient to fix the sense. It remains a description of corpus usage and not a definition from the standard, because this corpus may not reproduce normative text. Two factual corrections were made to this record's own text: the fault_reaction list on the two safety concepts has four entries and not five, and the identifier count of thirty-nine was verified by enumeration rather than carried forward. Nothing here asserts ISO 26262 conformity, certification, tool qualification, an ASPICE capability level, human approval, production authorisation or product verification credit. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false.

revision_history.author: safety_engineer
revision_history.description: Third issue. Adds identifier_vocabulary.migration_decision_2026_10_03 and nothing else: the forty-seven term definitions, the eleven absent terms, the fifteen dispositioned ambiguities and the ten per-identifier determinations are all carried forward byte for byte. The subject is the thirty-nine shared identifier strings. The previous pass declined the re-issue because four things naming the old identifiers were outside its boundary. Three of those four were cleared and the re-decision was taken on the evidence rather than on the boundary: README.md is editable and was re-measured, the two generated trees are regenerated from the corpus by renderers that are editable, and test_schemas.py was inspected and is not a blocker because it validates one literal sample payload against a schema and never reads the corpus. What remained were 465 occurrences in a graph-tool cache and 6 in OpenSpec text, four of which are already stale. The migration was still not performed, and the reason is recorded in full in the new entry: the corpus reads an unqualified identifier as the synthetic_reference copy, about nine hundred prose references depend on that reading, those references carry no profile and cannot be resolved mechanically, and renaming the synthetic side would make them resolve to the as_is copy instead while still reading as though they meant the synthetic one - with no validator output, because every renamed identifier would still resolve. A worked counterexample is recorded against FB2-SAF-TSC-000001's timing-budget closure argument, which is true of the synthetic copy of FB2-SAF-FSR-000003 and false of the as_is copy. The corpus is therefore left violating ID-RULE-004, openly, with the two governing positions - this record's 'do not renumber' and the task framing's ID-RULE-003 - recorded as contradicting each other and referred to a governance decision. The interim control added is a detector that reports the reuse as a medium finding on every run. Also re-anchored four source anchors that pointed at line numbers in docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py: all six corpus.py line anchors in this record were already stale at revision 2, off by between twelve and twenty-five lines, and two of them pointed at text that no longer exists in the file; the four whose target still exists are re-pointed at the true current line with the superseded value preserved, and the two dead ones are marked unverifiable rather than guessed at. No term, ambiguity, determination, digest or anchor content changed.

revision_history.author: safety_engineer
revision_history.description: Fourth issue. Records a governance decision that was referred at revision 3 and has now been taken, and reconciles two committed documents that formerly contradicted each other. The amendment: docs/artifacts/governance/corpus-policy.json amends ID-RULE-004 to state that an artefact identifier is unique WITHIN ITS PROFILE and that two records of different profiles may legitimately share an identifier string. amendment_id ID-RULE-004-A1, dated 2026-10-04, author safety_engineer. It records its previous text, its previous meaning, what it supersedes (the corpus-wide-uniqueness reading of ID-RULE-004 in its entirety; NOT ID-RULE-001, ID-RULE-002 or ID-RULE-003, which are unchanged), its rationale and the residual risk it relocates rather than removes. The contradiction this resolves: this record's identifier_vocabulary.adopted_convention said 'Do not renumber ... so a rename is not available as a repair', citing ID-RULE-001, while CORR-COV-021 in coverage-plan.json treated ID-RULE-003 as the sanctioned instrument and left the question referred. Document A said the corpus was non-conformant and no repair existed; document B said the corpus was non-conformant and a repair existed and was available. Both named the same rule text and reached opposite conclusions, and neither was subordinate to the policy, so neither could settle it. Which ruling now governs: the amended ID-RULE-004. This is route (b) - the route this record itself named as the cheaper and safer of the two at migration_decision_2026_10_03.what_would_settle_it, and the route that matches what the tool has always enforced. Route (a), migrating under ID-RULE-003, is declined on the evidence this record already recorded: renaming either profile inverts the unqualified-reference convention and makes roughly nine hundred prose references confidently wrong, with no validator able to detect it, because every renamed identifier would still resolve to exactly one live record. ID-RULE-003 is NOT invoked: no supersession, deletion or migration is being performed. The 39 shared identifier strings: no rename is required and none is permitted. They are conformant under the amended rule, each being carried by exactly one record per profile, which is what per-profile uniqueness requires. No string is carried by two records of the same profile; that is the condition the duplicate check reports as an error and it has never fired. The ID-RULE-001 reasoning that a rename was 'not available as a repair' is withdrawn as reasoning - ID-RULE-001 was never the bar - and the conclusion survives as a settled state rather than a deferral. Detection change: this record's interim control is withdrawn as a violation finding and replaced. corpus.py's cross-profile identifier reuse finding named ID-RULE-004 as violated; under the amended rule that is false, and a finding that names a rule the corpus does not violate is wrong at any severity. The check was repurposed rather than deleted, because the condition it carried contains a real defect the amendment does not address: the unqualified-reference convention is now load-bearing under the amended rule, and where the named id is carried by more than one live record a reader who does not know the convention has two candidates and no way to choose. The replacement reports unqualified references that are ambiguous for that reason, with the candidate records and the number of referring locations, report-only and not gated, because every id-keyed lookup resolves (profile, id) and no machine-read path is ambiguous. Fields changed and fields carried forward. Changed: revision, updated_at, identifier_vocabulary.artefact_identifier, why_it_is_a_vocabulary_problem, evidence[5] (establishes re-pointed at the amended text, previous wording preserved under superseded_establishes), adopted_convention, migration_decision_2026_10_03 (decision, plus new status, outcome and what_changed_on_2026_10_04 fields, and what_would_settle_it, interim_control and no_fabrication_statement rewritten to state the decision rather than refer it), the new identifier_vocabulary.supersession_reconciliation_2026_10_04, ambiguities_resolved[0] (why_the_convention, residual_ambiguity, settlement, what_was_settled, what_remains_open and evidence[3]), and limitations[1]. Added: this revision_history entry. Carried forward byte for byte: all forty-seven term definitions, all eleven absent terms with their measured counts, all fifteen dispositioned ambiguities other than VOC-AMB-001, all ten per-identifier determinations in per_identifier_determination, every digest, every source anchor other than the two re-pointed above, and every other limitation. One honest note on the withdrawn clause. migration_decision_2026_10_03 previously carried the sentence 'Nothing in this entry asserts that the identifier scheme now satisfies ID-RULE-004. It does not.' That sentence is withdrawn, because under the amended rule the scheme does satisfy it. It is recorded as withdrawn rather than quietly deleted, and it is the only change to the no-fabrication statement. Nothing here asserts ISO 26262 conformity, certification, tool qualification, an ASPICE capability level, human approval, production authorisation or product verification credit. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false.
